source.title: Kinglight Outdoor 2-in-1 LEDs: An Ideal Solution for High-End Outdoor Rental LED Displays
source.body_text: Nowadays, rental LED displays are widely used in commercial events like concerts, shows, exhibitions, brand launches, etc. Thanks to their flexible deployment and convenient installation, demand for rental LED displays continues to grow. As we all know, rental displays face frequently assembly, disassembly, transportation, and redeployment. This means rental LED displays demand higher on on both protection and maintenance efficiency. These two factors can directly affect their competitiveness in the market. To address these requirements, Kinglight has introduced two new 2-in-1 LEDs for outdoor rental displays: the 2391 and 2297 . Kinglight 2391 outdoor 2-in-1 LED sample plate Now let’s take a closer look at the key features of the two new 2-in-1 LEDs for outdoors and why they can be an ideal choice for high-end outdoor rental LED displays. Why we develop the two new outdoor 2-in-1 LEDs? For outdoor rental LED display projects, more and more end users are installing protective masks over LED modules. These masks mainly serve three purposes. 1. Absorb Impact and Improve Display Protection Rental LED displays need to be frequently assembled, disassembled, stacked, and transported. During these processes, bumps and scratches are difficult to avoid. A protective mask provides a physical barrier for the LEDs, helping reduce the risk of direct damage caused by external impact. 2. Reduce Ambient Light Reflection and Improve Image Quality A protective mask can help reduce reflections from ambient light and minimize glare and stray light interference. This can improve the display’s contrast and help maintain stable image quality in outdoor environments. 3. Block Dust and Rainwater to Extend Display Service Life Outdoor LED displays are often exposed to challenging environmental conditions, including dust and rain. A protective mask can help prevent moisture and dust from entering the display, contributing to a longer service life for rental LED displays. For these reasons, protective masks have become a common choice for many LED display manufacturers and end users. One of the key differences of Kinglight’s outdoor 2-in-1 LEDs is the snap-fit design designed on both sides of the LED package to accommodate protective mask installation . Let’s take a closer look at the product features and advantages. Kinglight 2391 & 2297 2-in-1 LEDs Effectively Improve Screen Protection and Maintenance Efficiency When conventional 2-in-1 LEDs or individual LEDs are used to build rental LED displays, protective masks are often secured with a large number of screws to ensure a tight fit. This approach can increase the structural complexity of the LED module, add assembly procedures, and reduce overall production efficiency. It can also make LED replacement and maintenance more time-consuming when a component fails. After repeated assembly and disassembly, the protective mask may become less securely fitted, reducing its protective performance and increasing overall maintenance costs. Kinglight’s outdoor 2-in-1 LEDs feature an innovative snap-fit design , which can significantly reduce the number of screws required and make screw-free protective mask assembly possible. Note: Screw-free protective mask assembly is a relatively aggressive application approach. Stability should be carefully evaluated according to the actual application environment and operating conditions. 1. S nap-fit design Improves Assembly and Maintenance Efficiency For LED display manufacturers: Higher efficiency and lower production costs The snap-fit design can significantly reduce the number of screws required for protective mask installation. This simplifies the assembly process, shortens production cycles, and frees up production capacity. It can also reduce the consumption of auxiliary materials such as screws, helping lower manufacturing costs. For end users: Easier maintenance and lower operating costs During display maintenance, the protective mask can be removed and reinstalled more easily. This simplifies maintenance operations, improves service efficiency, and can reduce long-term maintenance costs. 2. Optimized LED Height Helps Prevent Display Defects Caused by Mask Warping Take the 2391B LED as an example. Its overall height is 1.7 mm , which is 0.14 mm higher than the 1.56 mm height of conventional individual LEDs. The additional height provides sufficient space for the side snap-fit design. This helps prevent excessive pressure on the protective mask during installation, which could otherwise cause the mask to warp. By reducing the risk of mask deformation blocking the LED pixels, the design helps prevent potential negative effects on display performance. 3. 8-Pin Design with High Pulling Force for Better Impact Resistance Kinglight’s outdoor 2-in-1 LEDs use an 8-pin design , increasing the soldering contact area between the LED and PCB. The component can achieve a pulling force of 4–5 kg , while the pad adhesion is more than twice that of conventional individual LEDs. Combined with the impact-absorbing protection provided by the protective mask, the design creates a dual-layer protection system. This helps the LED withstand external impacts during assembly, disassembly, stacking, and transportation, reducing the risk of LED damage or detachment. It can also help reduce costs associated with LED replacement and on-site maintenance in rental applications. 4. High Brightness and Matte Finish for a Premium Visual Experience This series of LEDs supports a whole-display brightness output of 4000–5000 nits and uses high-quality imported encapsulation resin. When used together with a protective mask, the LEDs can provide a dual anti-reflection effect, helping suppress glare and stray light under strong outdoor lighting conditions. The result is a clearer and more stable visual output. The US$43 million investment in outdoor rental LED displays for Adele’s “Adele in Munich” concerts attracted worldwide attention and became a hot topic at the time. Conclusion Kinglight’s outdoor rental 2-in-1 LEDs combine several design features aimed at the demanding requirements of rental LED displays. The 8-pin, high-pulling-force design improves resistance to impact and helps enhance component reliability. The integrated snap-fit design can reduce the complexity and cost of protective mask assembly while improving installation and maintenance efficiency. At the same time, the LEDs offer high brightness and a matte, low-reflection surface , helping maintain image quality in bright outdoor environments. Compared with conventional individual LED solutions, Kinglight’s outdoor 2-in-1 LEDs provide advantages in component reliability, manufacturing efficiency, and overall lifecycle cost . They offer a practical component solution for building high-end outdoor rental LED displays .

examples.example_zh: Kinglight介绍用于户外租赁屏的2391和2297二合一LED。厂商表示，侧面卡扣设计可减少面罩装配所需螺丝；完全免螺丝方案仍须按实际环境和运行条件评估稳定性。文中4000–5000 nits为厂商给出的整屏亮度支持范围，不是对任意屏体配置的实测保证。
examples.example_en:
Kinglight describes its 2391 and 2297 2-in-1 LEDs for outdoor rental displays. The package has side snap-fit features intended to reduce the screws needed to attach a protective mask. Kinglight cautions that fully screw-free assembly requires stability evaluation for the actual environment and operating conditions. The article also gives a supported whole-display brightness range of 4000–5000 nits. This is a manufacturer statement about displays using these components; it does not establish measured brightness for an arbitrary finished screen.

Source: https://en.kinglight.com/blog/kinglight-2-in-1-led-for-outdoor.html

source.title: From LED Driver ICs to MBEyes Display Inspection: Macroblock and Juxin Present a Comprehensive Display Technology Portfolio
source.body_text: Macroblock and Juxin Photonics successfully held 2026 LED Display Symposium at the Shenzhen Marriott Hotel. In addition to the main-stage sessions, which focused on display industry trends and technology sharing, the exhibition area featured four major product highlights: MBS7263, a next-generation common-anode LED driver IC; MBS7986, a MOSFET IC designed for common-anode architectures; MBI5292, Juxin's classic flagship common-anode LED driver IC; and MBS7764, a next-generation common-cathode LED driver IC for MiP and COB applications. The MBEyes Display Inspection System was also showcased, demonstrating Macroblock’s expanded deployment in display quality inspection and end-customer services. Next-Generation Common-Anode LED Driver IC MBS7263 for Rental, Fixed Installation, and Transparent Displays 16 channels / Up to 32-scan / Current: 1–28 mA MBS7263 is Juxin's next-generation common-anode LED driver IC, developed for a broad range of applications including rental displays, indoor and outdoor fixed-installation displays, and transparent displays. Featuring 16 channels and support for up to a 32-scan design, MBS7263 enables flexible scan-number configurations according to customer requirements. It delivers high-specification display performance in low-scan designs while balancing image quality and system efficiency in high-scan configurations. For rental applications where fast installation, stable display performance, and high reliability are essential, MBS7263 supports LED display integration across different package types, offering end users greater flexibility. In scenarios that involve filming, its stable “Low Gray Refresh Multiplier” function helps reduce banding and flicker issues commonly seen when capturing low-brightness images, minimizing the need for post-production and accelerating the creation of secondary promotional content. In addition, fixed-installation and transparent display applications place high demands on brightness, grayscale performance, and image uniformity. MBS7263 further enhances visual performance by improving its ability to address coupling issues, helping displays present stable and refined images across diverse application scenarios. Left — MBS7263: Smooth, seamless gradient transitions. Right — MBI5292: The volcanic rock ’ s surface texture is reproduced with exceptional clarity, delivering a highly realistic visual effect. LED MOSFET IC MBS7986 | Designed for Common-Anode LED Driving Architecture 8 channels / Up to 2.5A output current per channel MBS7986 is an 8-channel MOSFET IC developed by Juxin for common-anode LED driving architecture. With an output current of up to 2.5A per channel, it helps mitigate issues that may arise in high-scan LED displays, including irregular module flicker during power-on, coupling interference, ghosting, and other artifacts that may emerge over extended operation. By enhancing image stability and overall display quality, MBS7986 helps reduce the risk of end users misinterpreting abnormal display behavior as a screen failure. MBS7986 also follows the pin configuration of mainstream MOSFET ICs, allowing customers to adopt and upgrade the solution more quickly on existing design platforms while improving development efficiency, supply flexibility, and display performance. Classic Flagship Common-Anode LED Driver IC MBI5292 | For High-End Visual Requirement Applications 16 channels / Up to 32-scan / Current range: 0.4–20 mA Macroblock's MBI5292 display, jointly showcased with LianTronics, fully demonstrated its flagship-level display capability for high-end visual performance applications. With 19-bit grayscale performance closely aligned with HDR EOTF, together with Macroblock’s unique “Low Gray Color Shift Removal” function, MBI5292 effectively compensates for color temperature shifts at low grayscale levels, enabling more accurate and natural presentation of dark details and color performance. Its “Low Gray Refresh Multiplier” function also helps reduce flicker and banding issues commonly seen in professional camera shooting and smartphone recording, improving camera friendliness and lowering post-production requirements. Whether viewed directly or captured through video cameras, MBI5292 helps LED displays deliver a more impactful and realistic visual experience. Common-Cathode LED Driver IC MBS7764 | Targeting MiP/COB Applications 16 channels / Up to 64-scan / Current range: 0.3–18 mA MBS7764 is Juxin's next-generation common-cathode LED driver IC, precisely targeting high-end display applications such as MiP and COB. Samples are expected to be available in Q4. In terms of specifications, MBS7764 can achieve a refresh rate of 15,360Hz under a full 64-scan design, helping enhance the overall performance of MiP and COB products in terms of high refresh rate, high image quality, and high stability, while further expanding the application coverage of common-cathode LED displays in the high-end market. MBEyes Display Inspection System | Display Health Report: Revealing True Specifications and True Performance How should the quality of a display be evaluated? Beyond the specifications listed on paper, visual performance is difficult to quantify and is often judged by the human eye, making human perception a significant variable. MBEyes uses an intelligent inspection process to help customers quickly understand display status. The inspection is divided into three major categories: basic specifications, optical indicators, and image quality, the latter of which has traditionally been the most subjective area. Through high-efficiency image capture, AI algorithm analysis, optical instruments, and related equipment, the system evaluates 21 items and provides scoring results. Through the on-site demonstration, MBEyes highlighted Macroblock’s comprehensive deployment beyond driver ICs, extending further into display quality management and customer services. The system helps display makers and customers verify product specifications with greater precision and efficiency, allowing the true specifications and true performance of displays to be clearly presented. Through the exhibition area at this symposium, Macroblock and Juxin presented a comprehensive product portfolio spanning common-anode and common-cathode LED driver ICs, MOSFET ICs, and MBEyes Display Inspection System. The showcase demonstrated the company’s technical strength in continuously responding to the display industry’s demand for high image quality, high refresh rates, high stability, and intelligent inspection. Looking ahead, Macroblock will continue to build on its core driver technology and work closely with industry partners to enable more precise, reliable, and competitive visual experiences for LED displays across a wider range of application scenarios. For information regarding the MBS product series , please contact Juxin Photonics (Shenzhen) Ltd. via email at info@jxsemic.com , or visit the company's official website for detailed product information: https://www.jxsemic.com/ .

Macroblock and Juxin presented a display technology portfolio at the LED Display Symposium. The source describes MBS7764 as Juxin’s next-generation common-cathode LED driver IC for MiP and COB applications. The article attributes MBI5292 differently in its introduction and detailed section, so this excerpt avoids resolving that ownership inconsistency.
